acceptance: A unit test with a fake connection whose COMMIT fails and leaves no active transaction gets the safe rolled-back result (return False), with the original error in the logged warning and the recorded failure
A unit test where rollback fails with a transaction still active still raises the unsafe RuntimeError
The run log of a failing sort shows the original engine error, not only the rollback message
description:
## Problem
benchbox/platforms/base/sorted_ingestion.py _execute_ctas_sort runs the constraint-preserving CTAS sort inside BEGIN/COMMIT. When DuckDB fails the COMMIT (measurement run 44348387772, duckdb SSB SF10 on a 16 GB GitHub runner, 2026-11-18: "Failed to commit: failed to pin block of size 256.0 KiB (11.1 GiB/11.1 GiB used)"), DuckDB has already aborted the transaction. The rollback then raises "TransactionContext Error: cannot rollback - no transaction is active", and the code raises RuntimeError "failed and could not be rolled back", treating a clean abort as an unsafe state. The run log shows only the rollback message; the out-of-memory cause is visible only in the chained traceback inside harness.json. The arm is aborted instead of recording a safe, rolled-back sort failure.

## Decision gate
Agent decision. Before the rollback, check whether the connection still has an active transaction (_connection_has_active_transaction already exists). If none, the engine has rolled back: take the existing "failed safely and was rolled back" path and log the original error. Keep the unsafe RuntimeError only when a transaction is still active and the rollback itself fails.

## Guardrails
- A real rollback failure with an open transaction must still raise.
- The original error text must appear in the warning and in the ledger failure record.
- No change to the sort itself or to DuckDB memory settings in this item.
